page: Amazon Web Services r7i.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned via the Nitro hypervisor. It runs on a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). The processor includes 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and supports vector instructions such as AVX-512, AMX-tile, and AMX-int8. The instance has a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and contains no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data demonstrates strong single-threaded capability, supported by a Geekbench single-core score of 2154.0 and strong compression throughput, including 33.68 GB/sec in gzip and 13.97 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 52.25 GB/sec for read and 50.43 GB/sec for write operations, while small cached reads register 689.3 GB/sec. Across multi-core routines, performance stabilizes into the median tier: stress-ng multi-core reaches 7070.01, multi-core Geekbench scores 8098.0, and PassMark overall CPU reaches 14256.46. While lightweight LLM prompt processing remains in the mid-tier, larger tasks such as 7B model generation show weakness at 7.97 tokens/sec due to the lack of hardware accelerators.

The configuration provides solid qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks requiring moderate compute density rather than extreme core counts. Because persistent disk relies entirely on remote storage, I/O-intensive designs must account for network volume latency. The r7i.2xlarge is well fitted for in-memory databases such as Redis, caching layers, mid-sized relational database engines, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.

Networking baseline throughput is rated at 3 Gbps, with zero local storage bundled and no discrete GPUs. The instance demonstrates strong single-threaded compute and compression metrics, while multi-threaded benchmarks and memory bandwidth consistently sit in the median range. Hardware accelerators such as AMX and AVX-512 enhance mathematical routines, but heavy machine learning tasks remain constrained without dedicated GPU hardware. With its abundant RAM relative to compute capacity, r7i.2xlarge is technically suited for in-memory caching platforms, enterprise databases, and memory-intensive backend services.
